noComponentSpecEither: No dedicated design-system component spec exists for this screen's status-annotation pattern either — the weakest evidentiary basis in the inventory (per the original visual audit's finding #4). The 'Completed/Current/Upcoming' annotation logic below is UX-spec-only.

layout.structure: path title/description -> path-level ProgressBar (if following) or 'Follow Path' CTA -> ordered, numbered member-course list (ALWAYS single-column, even at Large Desktop — a deliberate exception to the standard course grid, since sequence/order is the point)

content: numbered CourseCard list, each annotated Completed / Current / Upcoming

statusAnnotation.current: exactly ONE course at a time — the first not-yet-completed, enrolled-or-enrollable course, visually emphasized (border.focus outline or 'Continue here' label)
statusAnnotation.upcoming: default CourseCard treatment, NOT locked — out-of-order access is allowed in MVP; 'Upcoming' is informational sequencing only

rtlBehavior: sequence numbers/connecting lines mirror position but numbering (1->2->3) never reverses; status conveyed via icon+text+color together, never color alone
responsiveRules: single scrolling column at every breakpoint (no layout fork needed)
knownGaps: No showcase mockup AND no dedicated component spec exists — the weakest evidentiary basis in the screen inventory, per the original visual audit.
